name: Faro Cathedral (Sé)
blurb: Old-town cathedral with a tower whose views over the old town and the Ria Formosa lagoon are the highlight.

name: Bone Chapel (Capela dos Ossos)
blurb: Small chapel inside the Carmo church, almost entirely built from bones taken from an old monks' graveyard.

name: Old town (Centro Histórico)
blurb: Cobbled streets off the harbour lined with 18th-century houses in Portuguese and Moorish-influenced style; a slow walk.

name: Faro Jewish Heritage Centre
blurb: Heritage centre at the 1851 Jewish cemetery, the only surviving trace of Portugal's first post-Inquisition Jewish community.

name: Ria Formosa lagoon tours
blurb: Boat trips, birdwatching and kayaking in the Ria Formosa national park, sold by several tour companies from Faro and Olhão.

name: Boat to Faro beach (Praia de Faro)
blurb: Short boat ride to the long sandy Praia de Faro peninsula beside the airport; it stays quiet even in summer.

name: Restaurante Travessa
blurb: Cheap lunch spot with a €11 menu of the day; the 'tapas' plates are generous and the choice is wide.
priceText: €11 for the menu of the day

name: Faro Municipal Market (Mercado Municipal)
blurb: Local produce market with a supermarket in the basement and a few cafés in the same building; handy for picnic supplies.

name: Bar CheSsenta
blurb: Late bar decorated with Che Guevara photos, with a 20s–30s crowd, fair drink prices and karaoke on some nights.

name: Madeira Botanical Garden
blurb: Hillside gardens with more than 2,000 plant species, views over Funchal and a collection of parrots and parakeets.

name: São Lourenço Palace
blurb: Half fortress, half palace in mannerist style; the Noble Salon and Green Room are the highlights, plus the gardens.

name: Sé Cathedral (Funchal)
blurb: Funchal's most-visited monument, built 1493–1517 on royal orders, with a ceiling carved from local wood.

name: Museu CR7
blurb: Museum of footballer Cristiano Ronaldo's trophies, with his bronze statue out front; mostly for football fans.

name: Mercado dos Lavradores
blurb: Historic market with island fruit and vegetables on two levels and a separate fish hall; a good place to taste local produce.
when: Mon–Thu 07:00–16:00; Fri 07:00–20:00; Sat 07:00–15:00; closed Sun and holidays

name: Restaurante Beer Garden
blurb: Order the picado, a beef steak with chips meant for sharing; the normal size is plenty for two and cheap.
priceText: Picado normal size €10 (enough for two); bigger size €13

name: Vespas
blurb: Dance club on weekend nights, very popular with young people; the place for a late dance session.

name: Hole in One Madeira
blurb: The Irish pub option in Funchal, open daily until 02:00 for pints and an easy evening with the group.

name: Funchal Cable Car (Teleférico)
blurb: Gondola ride up from the city to Monte for big views over Funchal; a second cable car drops down to the Botanical Garden.
priceText: Adult one-way €16, return €22; children 7–14 half price; no student fare on the official page

name: Monte Toboggan
blurb: Wooden toboggan ride down a 2 km road from Monte, steered by traditional drivers; short, fun and very Madeiran.

name: Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel
blurb: Raphael Rooms, the spiral staircase and Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel ceiling; Rome's big must-see, so book a timed slot early.
priceText: €16 adults, €8 concessions; +€4 online booking fee; guided tour (€40 pp) often the only online option
when: Mon–Sat 09:00–18:00 (ticket office closes 16:00); closed 8 and 26 Dec

name: Pantheon
blurb: Ancient temple from 27 BCE, remodelled by Hadrian and later a church; the domed interior with its open oculus is the draw.

name: St. Peter's Basilica
blurb: Michelangelo's dome over the Vatican's great basilica; free to enter, though the security lines can be long.
when: Apr–Sep 07:00–19:00; Oct–Mar 07:00–18:00; closed Wed mornings for papal audiences

name: Museum of the Walls (Museo delle Mura)
blurb: Small museum inside Porta San Sebastiano on the Aurelian Walls, plus a walk along the top of the ramparts.

name: Testaccio Market (Mercato di Testaccio)
blurb: Neighbourhood food market with fresh produce, fish and flower stalls; stock up here for a picnic before sightseeing.

name: Pizzeria La Boccaccia
blurb: Trastevere pizzeria run by two Neapolitan brothers: a big slice and a huge cold beer for €5; it fills up with locals.

name: Big Mama
blurb: Trastevere's long-running blues and jazz club with Italian and international acts; shows usually start around 22:00.
when: Shows usually from about 22:00; check the programme

name: Be.Re
blurb: Prati craft-beer bar near the Vatican with many beers on tap and a few snacks, including trapizzino; open late daily.

name: Appian Way park bike ride
blurb: Rent a bike and cycle the Appian Way park, passing Roman tombs, ruins and stretches of the old city wall.

name: Duomo di Milano
blurb: Late-Gothic white-marble cathedral bristling with spires; the facade is free to admire, while the interior and roof cost extra.
priceText: Cathedral adult €3; roof by stairs €13, by lift €15; Baptistery of St John €3

name: The Last Supper (Santa Maria delle Grazie)
blurb: Leonardo's Last Supper in the refectory of Santa Maria delle Grazie; reserve months ahead or hope for a cancelled slot.
when: Book months ahead; cancelled tickets released from 08:15 daily

name: Museo del Novecento
blurb: Modern-art museum with Modigliani, Picasso, Morandi and Boccioni; the upper stairwell looks out over the Duomo roof.
priceText: Full €10, reduced €5, children 0–12 free; free first Sunday, and first and third Tuesdays from 2pm
when: Tue, Wed, Fri–Sun 10:00–19:30; Thu to 22:30; closed Mon; free from 14:00 on Tue 15 Dec

name: San Maurizio al Monastero Maggiore
blurb: Fully frescoed Renaissance church, mostly by Bernardino Luini; free to enter and a real must-see in Milan.

name: La Ravioleria Sarpi
blurb: Takeaway-only dumpling counter in the Sarpi area, often called Italy's best for Chinese dumplings; pork, beef or veg fillings.

name: Il Canarino
blurb: Traditional Milanese cooking such as risotto alla milanese and ossobuco; the five-course menu costs more but is worth it.

name: Bar Magenta
blurb: Aperitivo bar said to have coined the aperitivo; free nibbles come with drinks from about 19:00, best with a group.

name: Brasserie Bruxelles
blurb: Belgian beer bar with five beers on draught and about 50 in bottles; a good stop for beer lovers.

name: St Mark's Basilica (Basilica di San Marco)
blurb: Golden Byzantine-style basilica on Piazza San Marco; free to enter if you dress modestly, with fees for the upper museum and treasury.
priceText: Basilica free; upper museum €5; high altar €2; treasury €3

name: Doge's Palace (Palazzo Ducale)
blurb: Gothic seat of the Venetian doges; the Secret Itinerary guided tour reaches the administrative rooms and Casanova's former jail.

name: Gallerie dell'Accademia
blurb: Venice's leading art museum, strong on Venetian painters such as Bellini and Tintoretto; reservations cost an extra €1.50.

name: Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari
blurb: Huge Venetian Gothic friary church with Titian's Assunta and works by Bellini and Donatello; a cheap, big-name sight.

name: Cantine del Vino già Schiavi
blurb: Inventive cicchetti: pile a plate with what you like and staff pour a matching glass of wine; step outside by the canal if full.

name: Al Vecio Canton
blurb: Small, atmospheric Castello pizzeria famous for traditional pizza and seafood pasta at affordable prices.

name: Osteria da Filo
blurb: Cheap aperitivo bar popular with local students, with €2.50 spritzes and live music from time to time.

name: Chet Bar
blurb: Venice's nearest thing to a dive bar, open daily until 02:00, with cocktails better than the décor suggests.

name: Northern Giudecca canal walk
blurb: Long, sunny walk along the Giudecca canal, sheltered from winter northerly winds; you can stop by a gondola yard on the way.

name: Venice Casino (Casinò di Venezia)
blurb: Oldest gambling house in the world (1638), in a 15th-century building; entry is free when booked through selected hotels.
priceText: Entrance €10, free if booked at selected hotels

name: Cappella Sansevero
blurb: Baroque chapel with Giuseppe Sanmartino's Veiled Christ and other 18th-century sculptures; the marble masterpiece is the draw.

name: National Archaeological Museum (MANN)
blurb: Italy's top Roman archaeology museum, with finds from Pompeii, Herculaneum and Stabiae; it is one of Naples' must-sees.
priceText: €20; free with Artecard, on the first Sunday of the month, and for visitors under 18 or with a disability

name: Castel dell'Ovo
blurb: Naples' oldest castle on a rocky peninsula over the Gulf; free to enter, with bay views from the walls.

name: Royal Palace and Capodimonte Museum
blurb: Bourbon royal palace turned museum of 13th–18th-century paintings, from Titian and Caravaggio to Botticelli and El Greco.
priceText: Full €10; reduced €2 for visitors aged 18–25 (official site)

name: L'Antica Pizzeria da Michele
blurb: Iconic Margherita pizzeria with a thin, chewy crust; take a numbered ticket at the door and wait outside for it.

name: Pizzoteca Quartiere Spagnoli
blurb: Affordable, lively pizzeria in the Quartieri Spagnoli; pizza, drinks and the cover charge all cost little.

name: Mosto
blurb: Beautiful pub with an excellent beer and cocktail list and jazz on the speakers; a relaxed start or late stop.

name: Disco Mon Amour
blurb: Disco open Wednesday to Sunday nights; the weekend sessions run to about 04:00–04:30.

name: Pontile di Bagnoli
blurb: Free 900 m walk on a concrete pier over the Gulf of Pozzuoli, built for a steel mill that closed in 1993; sea views all the way.

name: Underwater Park of Gaiola
blurb: Protected marine area off Posillipo for snorkelling, diving or a glass-bottom boat trip; winter hours still run daily.

name: Pinacoteca Nazionale di Bologna
blurb: Bologna's main painting gallery: 13th–18th-century Emilian and Venetian art, with must-see works by Giotto, Raphael and Parmigianino.

name: Palazzo dell'Archiginnasio (Teatro Anatomico)
blurb: Former university palace whose wooden anatomy theatre is the highlight; cheap, but the theatre needs an online booking.

name: Basilica di San Petronio
blurb: Gothic basilica on Piazza Maggiore, planned as the world's largest church; only the long arm was finished, leaving the facade unfinished.

name: Museo Davia Bargellini
blurb: Quirky 17th-century palazzo museum with a marionette theatre, an 18th-century gilded carriage and antique keys; free.
when: Tue–Fri 09:00–13:00; Sat, Sun & holidays 10:00–18:30; closed Mon

name: Mercato di Mezzo
blurb: Covered food hall in the centre with a range of local stalls and tables; good value for lunch or dinner and busy all day.

name: Trattoria Da Vito
blurb: Down-to-earth trattoria with genuine Bolognese dishes from antipasto to dessert; popular with locals, service can be brusque.

name: Covo Club
blurb: Storied indie-rock and punk club since 1980, with concerts and DJ sets on Friday and Saturday nights.

name: The Link
blurb: Two-floor club for avant-garde electronic, techno and hip-hop gigs and DJ sets, with a small alternative bookshop inside.

name: San Luca portico walk
blurb: Climb the 600-plus arches of the portico from Porta Saragozza to the San Luca sanctuary for city views; the bus is the easy option.

name: Uffizi Galleries
blurb: Vasari-built palace of Renaissance painting, home to Botticelli's Birth of Venus; book a timed slot as the galleries get crowded.
priceText: Low season (10 Nov–20 Dec) adult €16, conc €6, combi €18; high season (21 Dec–9 Jan) adult €29; €4 booking fee included

name: Galleria dell'Accademia (David)
blurb: Michelangelo's original David and his unfinished Slaves, plus Florentine painting; photography is not allowed inside.

name: Ponte Vecchio
blurb: Medieval bridge over the Arno lined with shops, and the only Florentine bridge to survive WWII; free to walk across.

name: Piazzale Michelangelo
blurb: Hilltop square with the classic view over Florence and the Arno; walk up the Rampe di San Niccolò stairs from the river.

name: Trattoria Le Mossacce
blurb: Reliable old-town trattoria with simple traditional Florentine cooking, daily specials and bistecca alla Fiorentina.

name: I fratellini
blurb: Hole-in-the-wall street-food counter: cheap panini and wine, eaten standing on the pavement with your glass on the wall ledges.

name: Bamboo Lounge Club
blurb: Party club with techno and international DJs, two bars and VIP tables; popular with young adults and students.

name: Été
blurb: Lovely little café-bar with warm service and good local beer and wine; a cheap, relaxed stop.

name: Terme di Impruneta (thermal spa)
blurb: Thermal spa outside the city, fed by two natural springs; a warm-water escape from the centre.

name: Museo Egizio
blurb: Egyptian collection ranked second only to Cairo's, with many artefacts gathered by Drovetti; buying tickets online ahead is suggested.

name: Mole Antonelliana (National Cinema Museum)
blurb: Turin's 167 m landmark now houses the national cinema museum; the panoramic lift takes you up for city views.
when: Mon, Wed–Fri, Sun 09:00–19:00; Sat 09:00–22:00; closed Tue

name: Turin Cathedral (Duomo)
blurb: Late-15th-century cathedral; the Shroud chapel is reached on a Palazzo Reale tour, while the main church is free.

name: Santa Maria di Monte dei Cappuccini
blurb: Late-Renaissance Capuchin church on a hill above the River Po; free to enter, with the view over the river as a bonus.

name: Porta Palazzo market
blurb: Big street and indoor market for produce, ethnic groceries and second-hand goods; the best time to go is the morning.

name: Antica Bruschetteria Pautasso
blurb: Specialist in Piedmont dishes, including bagna cauda, the regional signature; a mid-range place to try the local classic.

name: Caffe Rossini
blurb: Café by day and late-night pub with music and a young crowd; open until 02:00 Mon–Thu and 04:00 Fri–Sat.

name: Lab Vittorio
blurb: Small, lively bar with good cocktails and tapas, plus a second bar on Via Mazzini; open late most nights.

name: Museum of the New Prison (Carceri Le Nuove)
blurb: Spooky guided tour of a former prison, with a descent into a WWII air-raid shelter; booking online is essential.
when: Tour daily 15:00; Sat and Sun also 17:00; air-raid shelter Sat–Sun 17:15

name: Cattedrale di Sant'Agata
blurb: Catania's imposing cathedral, home to the city's patron saint Agatha, on a lively baroque square.

name: Castello Ursino
blurb: 13th-century royal castle of the Kingdom of Sicily, now the civic museum with Greek and Roman finds from Catania.

name: Badia di Sant'Agata (dome tour)
blurb: Baroque church whose guided tours climb to the dome and terraces for city views; at €3 it is a cheap paid pick.

name: Benedictine Monastery of San Nicolò l'Arena
blurb: One of Europe's biggest monasteries, now a university faculty; the grounds are free and the interior is seen on a guided tour.
priceText: Exterior free; interior with guided tour €10
when: Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00; Sat 11:00–18:00; English tours at 13:00 and 16:00

name: La Piscaria
blurb: Big fish, fruit and vegetable market just off Piazza del Duomo; go in the morning, Monday to Saturday.

name: Dopo Teatro
blurb: Panineria with tables and a grill menu, known for grilled meats; open every day from 19:30 until very late.

name: Gammazita
blurb: Bohemian bar with wine, beer and cocktails and live music most nights; LGBTQ+ friendly, with a bookshop next door.

name: Vermut
blurb: Very lively vermouth bar with a huge selection of vermouths and other drinks; busy with young people in the evenings.

name: EtnaWay Mount Etna jeep tours
blurb: Guided jeep and 4x4 excursions up Mount Etna, picked up from Catania, Giarre or Taormina, with visits to summit craters.
